_doc: Anti-drift compass for the LOGBOOK DEEPWALK EXPANSION arc (Ian 2026-07-28: 'proceed to logbook roadmap next'). Companion to LOGBOOK_DEEPWALK_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md. tools/logbook_deepwalk_scoreboard.py reads this and emits a MEASURED % per phase and per LG class. EXPANSION means growing BOTH denominators: journeys x personas x states (board 1) and new LG dimension classes (board 2). A cell moves only on cited live evidence.
_phases_def: ground - map the surfaces, handlers, tables and caches the journey touches
walk - live-MCP journey walk carrying the full lens; requires >=2 personas AND >=2 states
observe - record friction with evidence (a clean walk is a real result, record it as such)
harvest - Engine B, at spoke 5 ONLY, for a friction the walk actually surfaced
resolve - fix, then LOCK with a gate; a fix without a gate is not done
_coverage_rule: A journey's W phase is 'done' only when walked in >=2 personas AND >=2 states. One-persona/one-state is the shallowness this arc exists to kill.

LB07.notes: WALKED LIVE 2026-07-28. Happy path clean end-to-end (offline insert -> queue -> reload keeps it queued -> reconnect -> DB row with correct auth_uid/hive_id; offline edit -> sync -> applied, updated_at touched by trg_logbook_touch_updated_at so the sync payload's missing updated_at is NOT a defect). DEFECT FOUND (S-error): a queued update matching 0 rows returns {error:null,status:204}, so `if (!error)` dropped the queued item and toasted '1 offline change synced.' while writing nowhere - proven by deleting the row server-side mid-offline, then confirming DB row absent + queue drained + success toast. 0 rows is the NORMAL RLS outcome (logbook UPDATE is owner-scoped on auth_uid, SELECT is hive-scoped). Same shape in the SHARED offline-queue.js drain() reaching 6 more surfaces. FIXED in both (read rows back, treat empty as unconfirmed, keep the worker's text, dead-letter, say so out loud); badge + feed-merge reconciled to the new _stalled state. HARVEST: web.dev offline-UX guidelines - 'never silent-fail, never false-success', 'on reconnect tell the user what synced + surface any conflict, do not silently drop'. GATED: tools/validate_offline_queue_confirm.py, teeth proven by reverting (FAILs on real pre-fix code at all 3 drain sites).

LB09.notes: Walked 2026-07-28 while driving LB7; saveEditFromForm exercised online AND offline as P-worker. FOUND: the page collapsed three different 0-row causes into one message ('Entry was modified by someone else, reload...'), which is right for a concurrent edit and WRONG for the other two - and in the ownership case no reload can ever help. Worse, 72 of Pablo's 571 entries had auth_uid IS NULL while UPDATE/DELETE require auth_uid = auth.uid(), so the UI offered Edit and Delete on rows the database would ALWAYS refuse (verified: an update of one applied nothing, no error). RESOLVED BOTH WAYS: (a) DATA - migration 20260728000000_logbook_auth_uid_backfill.sql binds auth_uid from the unambiguous worker_name->auth_uid mapping in hive_members (skips any name resolving to 2+ accounts rather than guessing, since attribution IS the DOLE/ISO trail); applied locally, 72 rows repaired, re-run is a no-op, and the previously-uneditable row now updates (1 row affected, live-verified). (b) CODE - one explainZeroRowWrite() resolver used by BOTH the online save and the offline drain, so the two paths cannot tell the worker different stories; all 3 reachable branches verified live (deleted / someone else's / concurrent-edit). HARVEST: NN/g error-message guidelines (state the cause + a real remedy), the same standard MK11 cites. GATE: the offline half is locked by validate_offline_queue_confirm.py. W stays PARTIAL at one persona. THIRD FIX (the small one that turned out not to be small): openEditModal is async and set _editingId only at the END, after an entry re-fetch and an await on renderReadingsFields(), while the save button stayed LIVE - so a fast tap ran saveEditFromForm() with _editingId still null, which offline enqueues under a null IndexedDB keyPath, THROWS, and strands the form with a permanently disabled button. Fixed at the source (hold the button with a 'Loading...' label for the whole populate, release it where _editingId is set, and hand it back on the not-found path) plus a defence-in-depth guard in saveEditFromForm. Both verified live: during the await the button is disabled/'Loading...' with _editingId null, after it is enabled/'Update Entry' with the id set; the guard toasts 'That entry is still loading' and recovers the button instead of stranding it.

LB17.notes: WALKED LIVE 2026-07-28 as Christine Dizon (worker in Manila, supervisor in Lucena). DEFECT FOUND: the server read is hive-filtered but the pending-queue MERGE was not, so after capturing offline in Manila and switching to Lucena the Manila entry rendered as a real card ('Pending sync') inside the Lucena feed - one tenant's work shown in another tenant's context. What is CORRECT and must stay: the queued row keeps its CAPTURE-time hive_id and syncs into THAT hive, not the current one (verified in the DB), which is why filtering is the right fix and re-homing would be wrong. FIXED (merge scoped to the active hive, reading hive_id from both the insert shape and the update shape - a first cut missed queued EDITS entirely because they carry hive_id inside `updates`). Re-verified all four ways: hidden in Lucena, still queued, visible again in Manila, lands in Manila on sync. GATED in validate_offline_queue_confirm.py (audit_queue_hive_scope); teeth proven on real pre-fix code. W stays PARTIAL: one persona only - the shallow-W guard is right to withhold full credit until a second persona walks it.

LG1.name: Mutation-contract parity
LG1.notes: Harvest = PDDA 2026-07-12: INSERT sets auth_uid, BOTH update paths omit it. DEFINED 2026-07-28 by the LB9 walk, and the rule is sharper than the original framing: an UPDATE omitting auth_uid is NOT itself the bug (the row keeps the auth_uid bound at insert, and the trg_bind_submitter_logbook trigger owns that). The real parity rule is that every mutating path must agree on how it CONFIRMS and EXPLAINS a write - which they did not: the online path checked rows and the offline drain did not, and each had its own story for the same failure. FIX PARTIAL: the confirmation and the explanation are now single-sourced (explainZeroRowWrite + the .select confirmation in both paths), and the auth_uid data gap that made the mismatch user-visible is backfilled. NOT DONE: the full enumeration of every logbook mutation site (saveEdit modal vs saveEditFromForm vs deleteEntry vs the PM mirror vs voice/photo capture) against one contract, and no detector or gate yet holds that parity - that is the class's next stage.

LG3.name: Offline-queue reconciliation — a queued write is a CACHE, and 0 rows is not 'synced'
LG3.notes: EARNED BY THE LB7 WALK 2026-07-28 (born from observed friction, per the arc's rule). RULE: a drain that removes a queued item must confirm the write actually affected a row - PostgREST returns error:null/204 for a 0-row update or delete, so branching on `error` alone destroys the worker's only copy and reports success. HARVEST: web.dev offline-UX guidelines ('never silent-fail, never false-success'; 'on reconnect tell the user what synced + surface any conflict needing their resolution, do not silently overwrite or drop'). SWEEP: all 3 drain sites platform-wide (offline-queue.js whCreateQueue+drain serving 6 surfaces, logbook.html syncOfflineQueue). FIX: read the rows back; empty = UNCONFIRMED not failed (on inventory_items a hive_id-NULL row is writable but not readable, so empty can also mean 'applied, not visible'); keep the item, dead-letter it, tell the user. GATE: tools/validate_offline_queue_confirm.py, registered, teeth proven by reverting to HEAD.

LG5.name: Transition tenant-integrity — data in flight carries CAPTURE-time identity
LG5.notes: EARNED BY THE LB17 WALK 2026-07-28. RULE: a queue/draft/filter holds the hive it was CAPTURED in; a hive switch must neither re-home it (data) nor display it outside that hive (glass). The hive arc locked the ROLE marker; this is the DATA-in-flight analog. Evidence: a Manila entry captured offline rendered as a live card in the Lucena feed after a switch, because the pending-queue merge was unfiltered while the server read was hive-scoped. FIX + GATE as recorded on LB17. SWEEP COMPLETE, and it came back CLEAN - a real result, recorded as such: every other queue surface (community, dayplanner, inventory, pm-scheduler, skillmatrix, asset-hub FMEA) only ENQUEUES; none reads the queue back to render a list, so none can leak a queued row across hives. logbook.html is the only page that merges pending items into its feed, which is why it was the only page with this defect - the same shape as the hive arc's finding that hive.html was the only page mutating role without a reload. Their payloads also carry capture-time hive_id, so the drain cannot re-home them either.

LG8.name: Mirror integrity, both directions
LG8.notes: OPENED ON MEASURED EVIDENCE 2026-07-28 (not yet walked). fault_knowledge.logbook_id has NO foreign key at all - the only FK on the table is hive_id. So deleting a logbook entry silently orphans its knowledge row, which stays in the RAG corpus and can be retrieved as knowledge citing an entry that no longer exists. Measured: 21 orphaned fault_knowledge rows live right now, dated 2026-07-20/21, none of them from this session's walk (checked explicitly) - so this is pre-existing drift against the PDDA arc's 529/529-valid measurement on 2026-07-12. Define partial: the rule is clear (a mirror must be reconciled on DELETE and AMEND, not only on CREATE; gate #27 locks CREATE lineage only), the detector and the fix decision - FK with ON DELETE SET NULL/CASCADE vs an application-side sweep - are open.
